content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are the meat of a chicken's wing, usually skinless and unseasoned. In this version they are precooked (boiled or baked) and ready to eat after reheating. The wings have a mild flavor, a slight sweetness and a crisp texture when properly heated.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a staple of American cuisine, famously served as “Buffalo wings”.
In Japan they are often glazed with teriyaki sauce, while in Korea they appear in spicy “yangnyeom” style.
Chicken wings contain more collagen than most other parts of the bird, which can be beneficial for skin and joints.
They have been served as a bar snack since the early 20th century.
The United States celebrates “National Chicken Wing Day” each year, dedicated to this dish.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Wings provide a good source of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: They supply niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Wings contain iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation, immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and moderate fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Wings contain more fat than most other chicken cuts; those monitoring fat intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium and preservatives
items.content: Precooked products may contain added salt and preservatives; people with hypertension or kidney issues should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Proper heating
items.content: Insufficiently reheated wings can harbor harmful bacteria; heat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat wings in the microwave, oven, or skillet. Serve them as a snack, in salads, tacos, or with sauces such as barbecue, cheese, or hot sauce. For extra crispness, bake at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep precooked wings refrigerated at 0–4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 2 months. Always reheat thoroughly before eating. Discard if the product develops an off‑odor, discoloration, or a slimy texture.
